fixture: heldout.json — 视觉自监督表示学习中的对比与非对比方法综述（SimCLR / MoCo / BYOL / SimSiam）
fixtureStatus: held-out: topic, sources and outline never used by M13.7.2–M13.7.7 (those used Transformer, DPR/RAG, LoRA/QLoRA, FedAvg/SCAFFOLD); zero prior occurrence of these papers in the repository

sources.retrieval: public arXiv abstract pages fetched 2026-10-12 (export API returned 429 at fetch time; the abs-page <meta name=citation_abstract> was used); every quote is asserted to be an exact substring of sources-abstracts.json before freeze
sources.verificationLevel: abstract — exact public abstract excerpts, manually scoped; NOT full-text grounding and NOT a production Grounding/Judge verdict

informationBudget.note: richer than every earlier fixture (538–900 unique quote chars); this is the real budget of four public abstracts, not padding. Sections with 0 assigned evidence (framing / conclude) may cite bibliography keys only as background (B group) — same rule as M13.7.7.

runtime: PiRuntimeAdapter, production buildSectionPrompt, toolPolicy read_only, 300 s per task, one shared writer session per arm (contextScope writing/acceptance/<arm>/sections), arms in independent projects/sessions

budget.taskUnit: one runtime.runAgent call = one Writer task (one section)
budget.requestUnit: assistant turns reported by PiRuntimeAdapter usage = underlying provider requests; recorded separately; a task that spends several turns is still one task but several requests — 20 tasks does NOT imply ≤ 20 requests
budget.retryPolicy: a task may be retried inside the 20-task budget only for a clear configuration error; the failed record is kept and reported; no retries for unfavorable content

arms.input: production buildSectionPrompt: full 12-record evidence snapshot to every section, 约350字 per section, original keyPoints task
per-section evidence partition (argumentUnits.evidenceIds) + per-section upper-bound length (180/400/400/320/160, lengthPolicy) + argument-task block (role, task, doNotExplain with owner section)
per-section evidence partition only; 约350字 and original instructions/keyPoints unchanged; no argument block

full evidence snapshot; per-section upper-bound length identical to glm-argument-unit (180/400/400/320/160) + the same lengthPolicy sentence; original keyPoints task; no evidence partition; no argument block

order: A → B first (stage 1); C and D only if stage 1 passes the gate; if B clearly fails, stop and attribute; no additional arms, seeds or prompt tuning
designLimits: not a full three-factor ablation: no H3-only arm, so B−C and B−D cannot be read as the independent causal contribution of H3 and interactions are not separable

the per-section upper bounds are shared by B and D (so B−D isolates evidence partition + argument block); they are smaller than 5×350 for framing/conclude sections, so D also carries a planning-level length redistribution, not only the upper-bound semantics
the shared lengthPolicy sentence necessarily names what not to pad with (restating, repeating limitations, quote-exceeding detail); it is identical in B and D and absent in A and C
single sample, single sampling run per arm; GLM outputs are not deterministic; no claim of stable generalization

evaluation.frozenBefore: first provider request of this round; markers, thresholds, checklist and these rules are not edited after outputs are seen (if a marker misses a legitimate spelling, both the marker count and the manual count are reported — the marker is NOT widened)
evaluation.detector: analyzeCrossSectionRedundancy defaults (minSentenceChars 12, minShared 6, containment ≥ 0.5, jaccard ≥ 0.2) from backend/dist/review/crossSectionRedundancy.js at the frozen HEAD
evaluation.primaryMetric: restatedCharShare (restated sentence chars / all sentence chars, outline-order later≈earlier)

gate.stage1Pass: B.restatedCharShare ≤ 0.70 × A.restatedCharShare (≥ 30 % relative drop) AND mustRetain checklist fully present AND no unknown cite key AND no new quote-exceeding factual claim that A does not also have AND no section that skips its task by writing short
gate.note: 30 % is a pre-registered engineering screen, not proof of generalization; shorter text alone is never counted as improvement

secondaryMetrics: concept carriers outside owner (full re-explanation vs one-sentence back-reference decided by reading)
cjk chars / cite commands / unknown keys / numbers outside quotes

manualReading.harmfulRestatement: a later-section sentence that re-explains a mechanism/result already fully explained in its owner section without adding the current section's own analysis; introduction scope summaries, one-sentence back-references ('如「X」一节所述'), comparison-axis reminders and conclusion echoes are NOT counted
manualReading.factAudit: every mechanism / result sentence with a cite is checked against the quote of the cited source; flags: partial-only support, uncovered technical detail, widened performance claim, inference written as fact, unverified claim kept behind a disclaimer
manualReading.shortWriteAvoidance: a section fails its task if a mustRetain item for that section is missing or if a comparison dimension listed in the task is not addressed

introduction: scope: self-supervised visual representation learning, two routes (negative-sample contrastive vs negative-free Siamese)
no own experiments / four abstracts as material
contrastive: SimCLR: learnable nonlinear transformation between representation and contrastive loss
SimCLR: benefits from larger batch sizes and more training steps
SimCLR: 76.5% top-1 linear evaluation (matching supervised ResNet-50) and 85.8% top-5 with 1% labels, scope as in quote
MoCo: contrastive learning as dictionary look-up; queue + moving-averaged encoder; large and consistent dictionary
MoCo: outperforms supervised pre-training counterpart in 7 detection/segmentation tasks (PASCAL VOC, COCO, others)
noncontrastive: BYOL: online network predicts target representation of the same image under a different augmented view
BYOL: target updated with slow-moving average of online network
BYOL: no negative pairs; 74.3% top-1 ResNet-50 linear, 79.6% larger ResNet
SimSiam: works without negative pairs, large batches, momentum encoders
SimSiam: collapsing solutions exist; stop-gradient essential to prevent collapsing
SimSiam: competitive results on ImageNet and downstream tasks
comparison: dimension: target-encoder update (moving average / slow-moving average / stop-gradient)
limitation: no own experiments, four abstracts only
limitation: numbers come from different models/settings → no performance ranking
partials E11 / E12 not written as fact
conclusion: relation of the two routes and what each changes in training
unified-protocol evaluation as future work, not completed contribution

factAuditRedFlags: MoCo removes / eliminates dependence on large batches (E12 partial)
negative-free methods outperform contrastive methods on all / any tasks (E11 partial)
cross-paper ranking from 76.5 vs 74.3 vs 79.6 (different models and settings)
SimSiam outperforms BYOL / MoCo / SimCLR (quote says 'competitive')

any mechanism detail not in the quotes: temperature, InfoNCE/NT-Xent, projection head dimensions, predictor network, EMA coefficient, queue size, batch size numbers, number of epochs, specific augmentations

noTuning: no prompt, fixture, marker, threshold or runner edits after the first glm-baseline request; unfavorable outputs retained; no selection among samples
